questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A preparer relies on a carryover figure taken from a previously filed return. What must be confirmed?
options: That the client's copy matches the original as filed
That the position relied upon has not been adjusted by examination or otherwise
That the earlier preparer held a valid PTIN
Nothing; reliance on a filed return is unqualified
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: How long may an individual carry forward an unused excess charitable contribution?
options: Indefinitely
Three succeeding years
Five succeeding years, in order of time
Twenty succeeding years
questions.explanation: An amount not used by the fifth succeeding year expires.
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: What happens to the character of a capital loss carried forward?
options: All carryovers become short-term
All carryovers become long-term
Short-term and long-term components carry forward separately and retain their character
Character is redetermined each year by the taxpayer
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer has net operating losses from 2016 and from 2021. How is the deduction computed?
options: The combined amount, limited to 80 percent of taxable income
The 2016 loss in full first, with the 80 percent limitation applied only to the 2021 layer
The 2021 loss first, because later losses take priority
Each layer limited to 80 percent separately
questions.explanation: Pre-2018 losses are allowed in full and are absorbed first.
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A disallowed passive activity loss is carried forward. How is it treated?
options: As a deduction against any income in the next year
As a capital loss in the next year
As a deduction or credit allocable to the same activity in the next taxable year
It expires after five years
questions.explanation: which is why suspended losses must be tracked activity by activity.
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Priya, who is single, carries a $27,000 long-term capital loss forward into 2026 and has no capital gains for the year. What may she deduct against ordinary income, and what carries forward?
options: $27,000, because a carryforward is fully deductible
$3,000, with $24,000 carrying forward as a long-term loss
$3,000, with $24,000 carrying forward as a short-term loss
Nothing, because carryforwards offset only capital gains
questions.explanation: Section 1211(b) caps the offset against ordinary income at $3,000 for the year regardless of the size of the carryforward, and the remaining $24,000 carries forward again, still long-term, because the character survives.
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Lucian sells 40 percent of his interest in a rental activity that carries several years of suspended passive losses, in a fully taxable sale to an unrelated buyer. What happens to the suspended losses?
options: They are released in full against this year's income
Forty percent of them are released
They stay suspended, allocable to the same activity, until the entire interest is disposed of in a fully taxable transaction
They are released, but only as a capital loss
questions.explanation: Section 469(g) frees a suspended passive loss only on a fully taxable disposition of the entire interest in the activity, and a partial interest is not the entire interest; the loss remains allocable to that activity under § 469(b).
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Under the reasonable cause and good faith exception to the preparer penalty, which of the following does Reg. § 1.6694-2(e) treat as an element of a normal office practice?
options: A review of the prior year's return
Independently verifying every position taken on the prior return
Obtaining a signed engagement letter before beginning work
Refusing to rely on any return prepared by another preparer
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6694-2(e)(4) lists a review of the prior year's return among the elements of the normal office practice that the reasonable cause and good faith exception rewards; reliance on a previously filed return is itself permitted under Reg. § 1.6694-1(e)(2).
questions.pageTitle: Use of prior years' returns for comparison, accuracy and carryovers

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which is not a minimum requirement for filing a return?
options: Providing a social security card
The taxpayer's date of birth as an intake fact
The identifying number of each dependent claimed
The taxpayer's filing status
questions.explanation: The number must appear on the return; the physical card need not be produced and may be supplied verbally or in writing.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer and both children hold ITINs. Which is available?
options: The child tax credit
The earned income credit
A dependency claim for each child
All of these
questions.explanation: An ITIN is a valid identifying number for filing and for claiming a dependent, but § 24(h)(7) and § 32(m) each require a social security number.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: What does IRC § 24(h)(7) require on the return as rewritten?
options: The qualifying child's social security number only
The taxpayer's social security number only
The taxpayer's social security number — or one spouse's on a joint return — and the child's
An ITIN for either the taxpayer or the child

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A qualifying child's social security number is issued two months after the return's due date. What is the effect on the earned income credit for that year?
options: The credit is allowed once the number is obtained
The credit is allowed if an extension was filed
The credit is not allowed for that taxable year
The credit is allowed at half the amount
questions.explanation: Section 32(m) requires the number to be issued on or before the due date for filing the return for the taxable year.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Publication 1345 says an ERO should ask a taxpayer not known to them for two forms of identification. What is the status of that guidance?
options: A statutory condition of filing a return
A preparer safeguard against identity theft refund fraud
A requirement only for paper returns
A condition of claiming any refundable credit
questions.explanation: It is addressed to the provider as a fraud safeguard, not to the taxpayer as a filing requirement.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty that IRC § 6109(a) places on a person making a return?
options: Producing the physical social security card to the preparer
Furnishing their own identifying number to a person who must show it on another return
Obtaining an identity protection PIN before filing
Presenting two forms of photo identification
questions.explanation: IRC § 6109(a) requires a person to include the prescribed identifying number on their return, to furnish their number to a person who must show it on another return, and to request and include the number of any other person about whom they make a return; producing the card and the two-forms-of-identification step are Publication 1345 safeguards, not statutory duties.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Marisol married in October 2026 and e-files her first return under her new surname, but has not updated her record with the Social Security Administration. The return rejects. According to Publication 1345, what is the most likely cause?
options: The IP PIN was omitted
The Name Control — the first four significant letters of the surname as the Social Security Administration records it — does not match
Her filing status changed during the year
A newly married taxpayer must paper-file the first joint return
questions.explanation: Publication 1345 identifies the wrong name associated with a number as a leading cause of rejected returns, and the Name Control mismatch most often arises for a newly married taxpayer whose SSA record has not been updated; the number must be transcribed exactly as the source document shows it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Teodoro's qualifying child holds a social security number that was issued before the due date but solely for non-work purposes. Teodoro claims the earned income credit for 2026. What is the result?
options: The credit is allowed, because the number was issued in time
The credit is allowed at half the usual amount
The credit is not allowed, because a number issued solely for non-work purposes does not satisfy the identification requirement
The credit is allowed if the child later obtains a work-authorised number
questions.explanation: IRC § 32(m) requires a social security number issued by the Social Security Administration other than one issued solely for non-work purposes, and existing on or before the due date; both conditions do work, and the non-work condition fails here regardless of timing.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which is not a means of ending lawful permanent resident status?
options: A voluntary written statement of intent to abandon, filed with the registration card
Failing the substantial presence test
Administrative termination by the immigration authority
A final judicial order of exclusion or deportation
questions.explanation: Resident status is deemed to continue unless rescinded or administratively or judicially determined to have been abandoned; the substantial presence test is a separate route into residency.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An individual was present 90 days two years ago and 120 days last year. What is the minimum current-year presence that meets the substantial presence test?
questions.explanation: The prior years contribute 15 and 40, leaving 128 of the 183 required — and 128 also clears the separate 31-day condition.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which is not a requirement for obtaining an adoption taxpayer identification number?
options: The child is eligible to be claimed as a dependent
The child's SSN cannot be obtained from the birth parents despite reasonable attempts
A foreign adoption has a Permanent Resident Alien Card or Certificate of Citizenship
The adoption process has been completed
questions.explanation: The number exists for a pending adoption; completion is what ends it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An individual is present in the United States for 40 days in the current year and has a weighted three-year total of 200 days. What is the result?
options: Resident alien, because the weighted total exceeds 183
Resident alien, because presence exceeded 31 days
Nonresident alien, unless the closer connection exception is claimed
Resident alien only if a first-year election is made
questions.explanation: Both conditions are met — 40 days exceeds the 31-day minimum and the weighted total exceeds 183 — so the test is satisfied.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which of these does an ITIN do?
options: Authorise the holder to work in the United States
Qualify the holder for the earned income tax credit
Serve as identification outside the federal tax system
Provide a taxpayer identification number for federal tax purposes
questions.explanation: The IRS states that an ITIN does none of the other three.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Zara Mbeki-Sørensen meets the substantial presence test this year with 150 days of presence, keeps her tax home in Denmark and has a closer connection there, but in August filed an application for adjustment of status to lawful permanent resident. Can she use the closer connection exception?
options: Yes, because her tax home and closer connection are both in Denmark
Yes, provided the application is still pending at year-end
No, because taking steps toward lawful permanent residence during the year forfeits the exception
No, because the exception is available only to exempt individuals
questions.explanation: IRC § 7701(b)(3)(C) withdraws the closer connection exception from anyone who, at any time during the year, had an application for adjustment of status pending or otherwise took steps toward lawful permanent residence.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Lucía arrives on a work visa on 1 June, is present every day afterwards and meets the substantial presence test for the year. She holds no green card and was not present in the two prior years. For which part of the year is she a resident alien?
options: The entire calendar year, because the test is met for the year
From 1 June, her residency starting date, producing a dual-status year
From 1 January of the following year
From the day her weighted count reached 183
questions.explanation: IRC § 7701(b)(2)(A) treats a first-year resident as a resident only for the portion of the year beginning on the residency starting date — for a substantial presence case, the first day of presence in the year — which produces a dual-status year.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Kwame has been in the United States on a student visa for almost every day of the last three years and holds no green card. Before running the weighted day count, what must his adviser check?
options: Whether his weighted three-year total exceeds 183
Whether he was present at least 31 days in the current year
Whether he is an exempt individual whose days are not counted at all
Whether he has made a first-year election
questions.explanation: A student is an exempt individual under IRC § 7701(b)(5)(A)(iii), and days on which an individual is an exempt individual are excluded from the substantial presence count, so the exemption is checked before the arithmetic rather than after.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Under the substantial presence test, which combination of facts, by itself, is sufficient to make a non-citizen a resident alien for the current year (absent an exception)?
options: Present in the U.S. for 20 days in the current year and 200 days in the prior year
Present in the U.S. for 40 days in the current year, with a weighted three-year total (current year plus one-third of the prior year plus one-sixth of the year before that) of at least 183 days
Present in the U.S. for any number of days in the current year, as long as the taxpayer holds a valid visa
Present in the U.S. for 100 days in the current year only, regardless of prior years
questions.explanation: The substantial presence test requires at least 31 days of presence in the current year AND a weighted total of at least 183 days across the current year (full weight), the prior year (one-third weight), and the year before that (one-sixth weight). A bare 20-day current-year count fails the 31-day threshold outright, no matter the weighted total.
questions.pageTitle: Residency status and/or citizenship (e.g., citizen, visas, green cards, resident alien or non-resident alien, ITIN)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer was a nonresident alien for part of the year and became a resident alien partway through the same year, with no election to be treated differently. What best describes this taxpayer's filing position for that year?
options: The taxpayer files only Form 1040-NR for the entire year
The taxpayer files only Form 1040 for the entire year, exactly as a full-year resident would

The taxpayer is a dual-status alien for the year, generally reporting the resident period and nonresident period under their respective rules, with restrictions such as not using the standard deduction for the dual-status return
The taxpayer chooses freely which single return to file for the whole year with no restrictions
questions.explanation: A taxpayer who is a nonresident alien for part of the year and a resident alien for the rest is a dual-status alien. The return reflects both periods, and dual-status filers face specific restrictions — for example, they generally cannot claim the standard deduction — that don't apply to a taxpayer who was a resident alien for the full year.
questions.pageTitle: Residency status and/or citizenship (e.g., citizen, visas, green cards, resident alien or non-resident alien, ITIN)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An individual is not eligible for a Social Security number but needs a U.S. taxpayer identification number to be listed on a return, for example as a nonresident alien spouse. What is true of the ITIN issued in this situation?
options: It authorizes the holder to work legally in the United States
It establishes eligibility for the earned income tax credit
It confers a particular immigration status on the holder
It is issued solely for federal tax reporting purposes and does none of the above
questions.explanation: An ITIN is issued strictly to allow federal tax reporting for people who need a taxpayer identification number but aren't eligible for a Social Security number. It does not authorize work, does not by itself establish eligibility for the earned income tax credit (which requires a valid SSN), and does not confer or change immigration status.
questions.pageTitle: Residency status and/or citizenship (e.g., citizen, visas, green cards, resident alien or non-resident alien, ITIN)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An individual dies on 1 May. The estate adopts a fiscal year ending 30 June. When is Form 1041 due, absent an extension?
options: 15 April
15 July
15 August
15 October
questions.explanation: A fiscal-year return is due the fifteenth day of the fourth month following the close of the fiscal year; April is the calendar-year date.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: The filing requirement under IRC § 6012 is measured against what?
options: Taxable income
Adjusted gross income
Gross income
Net income after credits
questions.explanation: A taxpayer whose deductions eliminate the liability may still be required to file.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: What does a timely filed Form 4868 obtain?
options: Six months more to file and to pay
An automatic six-month extension of time to file only
Four months to file, extendable by a further two
A waiver of interest on the unpaid balance
questions.explanation: Interest runs from the original due date and the failure-to-pay addition continues to accrue.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A United States citizen whose tax home and abode are outside the United States has what extension without applying?
options: None; an application is always required
To the fifteenth day of the sixth month following the close of the taxable year, for filing and
Six months, running after the ordinary extension expires
To 15 April of the second following year
questions.explanation: and the ordinary six-month extension runs concurrently with it, not after it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A filing deadline falls on a day that is a legal holiday in the taxpayer's state but not in the District of Columbia. What is the effect?
options: The deadline moves to the next business day
The deadline is unchanged
The deadline moves only for taxpayers resident in that state
The taxpayer must file early
questions.explanation: IRC § 7503 defines "legal holiday" as a legal holiday in the District of Columbia.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Beatriz is 67 and married. For 2026 she files a separate return from her husband. May she claim the deduction for seniors on that return?
options: Yes, since she attained 65 before the close of the year
Yes, but at half the amount
No, because a married taxpayer may claim it only on a joint return
No, because the deduction expired after 2025
questions.explanation: Section 151(d)(5)(C) allows the deduction only on a joint return for a married taxpayer, and also requires the qualified individual's social security number on the return; it runs for taxable years beginning before 1 January 2029.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A preparer relies on 2024 material stating that the personal exemption amount returns in 2026, so the filing threshold becomes the exemption plus the standard deduction. Is that right?
options: Yes, the zero exemption applied only to 2018 through 2025
No, the zero exemption was made permanent, so the threshold remains the basic standard deduction
Yes, but only for taxpayers with dependents
No, the exemption was replaced by the deduction for seniors for everyone
questions.explanation: Section 70103(a) of Public Law 119-21 amended IRC § 151(d)(5) so the zero exemption applies to all taxable years beginning after 2017, and the IRC § 6012(a)(1) threshold continues to collapse to the applicable basic standard deduction.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A calendar-year individual has a valid extension to 15 October, and in that year 15 October falls on a Sunday. When is the extended return timely filed?
options: On or before Friday 13 October, the last business day before the deadline
On or before Sunday 15 October, since the extension does not move
On or before Monday 16 October
On or before Tuesday 17 October, regardless of the calendar
questions.explanation: IRC § 7503 makes an act timely if performed on the next succeeding day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or District of Columbia legal holiday, and the last day is determined including any authorised extension of time, so the extended deadline moves to Monday.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A calendar-year individual taxpayer files Form 4868 by the original due date and it is accepted. What does this extension actually accomplish?
options: It extends both the time to file and the time to pay any tax owed
It extends the time to file the return but not the time to pay any tax owed
It extends the time to pay but requires the return to still be filed on the original due date
It waives any failure-to-pay penalty regardless of when the balance is paid
questions.explanation: Form 4868 grants an automatic extension of time to file (typically six months), but it does not extend the time to pay. Tax owed is still due by the original due date, and interest and the failure-to-pay penalty generally continue to accrue on any unpaid balance from that date.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A self-employed taxpayer has $500 of net self-employment earnings for the year and no other income. Which statement is correct about the filing requirement?
options: No return is required because total income is below the standard filing-threshold amounts
A return is required because net self-employment earnings of $400 or more trigger a filing requirement regardless of the general gross-income thresholds
A return is required only if the taxpayer also owes income tax on the amount
A return is required only if the taxpayer received a Form 1099-NEC for the income
questions.explanation: Net self-employment earnings of $400 or more create a filing requirement on their own, to capture self-employment tax, independent of the general gross-income filing thresholds that apply to wage and other income.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer is claimed as a dependent on someone else's return and has only unearned income (interest and dividends) for the year. Compared to a taxpayer who is not claimed as a dependent, how is this dependent's own filing requirement determined?
options: Using the same gross-income thresholds that apply to non-dependents
Using separate, generally lower thresholds specific to dependents, based on earned and unearned income
There is never a filing requirement for a dependent regardless of income
Only the person who claims the dependent has any filing obligation related to that income
questions.explanation: A dependent's filing requirement is measured against its own set of thresholds (which differ for earned income, unearned income, and combinations of the two), not the general thresholds that apply to a taxpayer who isn't claimed as a dependent.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which is not a requirement for head of household status?
options: The individual is unmarried or considered unmarried on the last day of the year
A qualifying dependent parent lives at the same residence as the taxpayer
The individual paid more than half the cost of keeping up the home
A qualifying person lived in the home for more than half the year
questions.explanation: For a parent, the test is whether the taxpayer maintains the household that is the parent's principal place of abode — the parent need not live with the taxpayer.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer's spouse died in 2024. For which years may the taxpayer file as a qualifying surviving spouse, assuming a dependent child in the home and no remarriage?
options: 2024 only
2025 through 2027
questions.explanation: A joint return is available for the year of death itself; surviving spouse status covers the two taxable years after it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: When is marital status determined?
options: On the first day of the taxable year
On the last day of the taxable year, or at the time of death if a spouse dies during the year
By the number of months married during the year
On the date the return is filed

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A married taxpayer files separately, has a child living with her all year, pays all household costs, and her husband moved out on 12 August. May she file as head of household?
options: Yes; she paid all the costs and the child lived with her
Yes, because they are separated in fact
No; the spouse must not have been a member of the household during the last six months of the year
No; head of household is never available to a married person
questions.explanation: The spouse's departure must precede the final six months, so a departure after 30 June fails the test for that year.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Neither spouse will sign a joint return and one spouse is a nonresident alien for part of the year. What follows?
options: A joint return may still be filed if the alien spouse consents
No joint return may be made, and the other spouse may be treated as not married for head of
Both spouses must file as single
The couple must file jointly by default
questions.explanation: Section 6013(a)(1) bars the joint return; § 2(b)(2)(B) treats the taxpayer as not married for head of household.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Ingrid's husband died in 2025. Her dependent son lives with her all year and she pays every cost of the home. On 20 December 2026 she remarries. What is her filing status for 2026?
options: Qualifying surviving spouse, because the death was within the two preceding years
Married filing jointly or separately with her new husband
Head of household
Single
questions.explanation: IRC § 2(a)(2)(A) makes surviving spouse status unavailable if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, and under § 7703(a) marital status is determined at the close of the year, so she is married for the whole of 2026.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Beatriz is 67 and married. For 2026 she and her husband file separate returns. May she claim the new deduction for seniors on her separate return?
options: Yes, at half the amount available on a joint return
Yes, in full, because she has attained age 65
No; a married taxpayer may claim it only on a joint return
No; the deduction is available only to unmarried taxpayers
questions.explanation: IRC § 151(d)(5)(C), added by Public Law 119-21 for taxable years beginning before 2029, attaches a filing-status condition to the deduction for seniors: a married taxpayer may claim it only on a joint return, which adds an item to the joint side of any married-filing-separately comparison.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Deshawn and Marguerite file a joint return for 2026. Deshawn alone earned every dollar of the income and omitted some of it. Who is liable for the resulting deficiency?
options: Deshawn only, because he earned the income
Each spouse for a proportional share based on their own income
Each spouse for the entire liability
Marguerite only if she signed the return knowing of the omission
questions.explanation: IRC § 6013(d)(3) provides that on a joint return the tax is computed on aggregate income and the liability is joint and several, so each spouse is liable for the whole of it; this is the fact behind every innocent spouse case.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Dana's spouse died in 2024. Dana has not remarried and pays over half the cost of keeping up a home that is the principal residence of Dana's dependent child for all of 2026. Which filing status may Dana use for the 2026 tax return?
options: Single
Head of household
Qualifying surviving spouse
Married filing jointly
questions.explanation: Qualifying surviving spouse status is available for the two tax years following the year of a spouse's death (here, 2025 and 2026) if the taxpayer has not remarried, maintains a home that is the principal residence of a dependent child for the whole year, and paid over half the cost of keeping up that home. Head of household would apply once the two-year window has passed.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer filing status (e.g., single, head of household)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A married couple lives together all year and wants to file separate returns. If one spouse itemizes deductions on Form 1040, what is required of the other spouse?
options: The other spouse may freely choose to itemize or claim the standard deduction
The other spouse must also itemize, even if it produces a $0 itemized total
The other spouse must claim the standard deduction
The couple must instead file a joint return
questions.explanation: Under MFS, if one spouse itemizes, the other spouse's standard deduction is treated as zero — the other spouse must also itemize (even if that means claiming little or nothing), rather than being free to claim the standard deduction.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer filing status (e.g., single, head of household)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which of the following, by itself, disqualifies a taxpayer from claiming head of household status?
options: Being unmarried at the end of the year
Paying more than half the cost of keeping up the home
Living with a qualifying person for more than half the year
Filing a joint return with a spouse for the year
questions.explanation: Head of household requires the taxpayer to be unmarried (or considered unmarried) at year end and to file their own return; filing a joint return with a spouse is fundamentally incompatible with claiming head of household for that year. The other three items are requirements, not disqualifiers.
questions.pageTitle: Taxpayer filing status (e.g., single, head of household)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Marisol sold vintage clothing through an online marketplace in 2026, collecting $16,500 across about 150 transactions. No Form 1099-K arrived. How much of the $16,500 is gross income?
options: None, because the marketplace was not required to report it
Only the amount above the reporting threshold
All of it, as gross income derived from business
None, unless the transaction count also exceeds the threshold
questions.explanation: IRC § 6050W(e) sets conditions on the settlement organization's filing duty, requiring a report only where both the dollar and transaction-count thresholds are exceeded; falling under them has no bearing on the taxpayer, and the receipts are gross income derived from business under IRC § 61(a)(2).
questions.pageTitle: Sources of all worldwide taxable and nontaxable income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Ravi's municipal bond fund statement shows $5,000 of interest, of which the fund reports $250 as interest on private activity bonds that are not qualified bonds. What is includible in gross income, and what else must be reported?
options: Nothing is includible and nothing is reported
$250 is includible, and the remaining $4,750 is still reported as tax-exempt interest
All $5,000 is includible because the fund holds more than one bond
Nothing is includible, but the $250 is reported as tax-exempt interest
questions.explanation: IRC § 103(a) excludes interest on a State or local bond, but IRC § 103(b) withdraws the exclusion for a private activity bond that is not a qualified bond; the excluded portion is still reported because other computations, such as the IRC § 86 formula, reference tax-exempt interest.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of all worldwide taxable and nontaxable income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Under a divorce instrument executed in 2022, Helena receives $1,500 a month in alimony from her former spouse. How does she treat the payments on her 2026 return?
options: Includes them in gross income as an enumerated item in IRC § 61(a)
Includes them only to the extent they exceed her former spouse's deduction
Excludes them, because alimony was struck from IRC § 61(a) for post-2018 instruments
Includes half of them, as with social security benefits
questions.explanation: Alimony was struck from IRC § 61(a) by Pub. L. 115-97 § 11051(b)(1)(A), so for a post-2018 instrument the recipient does not include it; only a pre-2019 instrument not modified to adopt the new rule keeps the old treatment.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of all worldwide taxable and nontaxable income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Lucas, a sole proprietor, paid $8,400 for a health policy covering himself and his wife for all of 2026. From 1 October his wife's employer offered her subsidized coverage, which she declined. For which months is the IRC § 162(l) deduction available?
options: All twelve, because she never enrolled in the employer plan
None, because eligibility for a spouse's employer plan at any point in the year defeats the deduction
January through September only
October through December only
questions.explanation: IRC § 162(l)(2)(B) denies the deduction for any calendar month in which the taxpayer is eligible to participate in a subsidized plan maintained by an employer of the taxpayer or the spouse; the test is eligibility rather than enrolment, applied month by month.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of applicable exclusions and adjustments to gross income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: IRC § 62(a) does not name the deduction for one-half of self-employment tax. How does it nonetheless reduce adjusted gross income?
options: It is an itemized deduction that a non-itemizer may also claim
It is treated as attributable to a trade or business, so it arrives through the trade or business paragraph of IRC § 62(a)
It is an exclusion from gross income rather than a deduction
It reduces the self-employment tax itself, not adjusted gross income
questions.explanation: IRC § 164(f)(1) allows one-half of the § 1401 taxes, other than the § 1401(b)(2) additional Medicare tax, as a deduction, and IRC § 164(f)(2) directs that it be treated as attributable to a trade or business, so it enters adjusted gross income through IRC § 62(a)(1).
questions.pageTitle: Sources of applicable exclusions and adjustments to gross income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Owen teaches grade 6 and spent $1,300 of his own money on classroom supplies in 2026. His school reimbursed $250 under an arrangement that excluded that amount from his income. Before applying the dollar cap, what is the base for his educator expense deduction?
questions.explanation: IRC § 62(d)(2) allows the § 62(a)(2)(D) deduction only to the extent expenses exceed the amounts excludable from gross income for the same items, so the reimbursed $250 comes off first, leaving $1,050 before the indexed cap.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of applicable exclusions and adjustments to gross income

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Theo is 20, a full-time student claimed by his parents, blind, and earned $3,000 at a part-time job in 2026. Which statement about his standard deduction is correct?
options: The dependent cap limits his entire standard deduction, so no blindness increment is allowed
The cap limits only his basic amount, and the blindness increment is added on top
He gets no standard deduction because a dependent cannot claim one
He gets the full single basic amount because blindness lifts the cap
questions.explanation: IRC § 63(c)(5) caps a dependent's basic standard deduction at the greater of the floor amount or the allowance plus earned income, but it limits the basic amount only, so the § 63(f) increment for blindness sits on top of the capped figure.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Nadine and her husband filed separate returns for 2026 and each elected to itemize. Nadine now wants to change her election and take the standard deduction for that year. What does the change require?
options: Nothing beyond an amended return, since the election is freely revocable
Her husband's consent to her change only
Her husband's consistent change of his own election and both spouses' written consents to assessment
The change is not permitted once either spouse's return has been filed
questions.explanation: IRC § 63(e)(3) allows the election to be changed after filing, but where a spouse filed separately for the corresponding year the change requires that spouse's consistent change and both written consents to assessment.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Marcus takes the standard deduction for 2026. He has qualified tip income, qualified overtime compensation, interest on a loan for a passenger vehicle, and home mortgage interest. Which of these can he not deduct without electing to itemize?
options: The qualified tips
The qualified overtime compensation
The passenger vehicle loan interest
The home mortgage interest
questions.explanation: IRC § 63(b)(1)–(7) lists the deductions a non-itemizer takes alongside the standard deduction, including § 224 tips, § 225 overtime and the passenger-vehicle-loan interest exception; qualified residence interest falls within the residual definition of itemized deductions in IRC § 63(d) and needs the election.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which does not meet the age requirement to be a qualifying child?
options: A 17-year-old single mother
A 30-year-old with a permanent and total disability
A 28-year-old full-time student
A 9-year-old
questions.explanation: A student must be under 24; there is no age limit for an individual permanently and totally disabled at any time during the year.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A child resided with Parent A longer than with Parent B during the year, and Parent A also has the higher adjusted gross income. The parents do not file jointly and both claim the child. Who prevails?
options: Both may claim the child
Parent A
Parent B
Neither may claim the child
questions.explanation: decided by residence, not income. Income is reached only where residence is equal.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A dependent has $10,000 of taxable income and $4,000 of tax-exempt income, saves $1,000 and spends the rest on her own support. What is the minimum the taxpayer must provide?
questions.explanation: She applied $13,000 to her own support; the taxpayer must exceed half of total support, which means exceeding $13,000.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which individual may not be claimed as a dependent?
options: A foreign exchange student living in the taxpayer's home
A foreign-born adopted child living with the taxpayer as a member of the household
A resident of Canada
A United States resident alien
questions.explanation: The citizenship and residency gate admits residents of the United States, Canada and Mexico, with a narrow exception for an adopted child.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An 18-year-old mother who can be claimed as a dependent by her parents lives with them and her own child. Who may claim the child?
options: Both the grandparents and the teenage parent
Neither
Only the grandparents
Only the teenage parent
questions.explanation: An individual who is a dependent of another taxpayer is treated as having no dependents — though the grandparents must also clear the tiebreaker rule that applies where no parent claims.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer provides over half of her mother's support. The mother lives in her own apartment and has 7,800 dollars of gross income for 2026. May the taxpayer claim her as a dependent?
options: Yes, because the relationship and support tests are both met
No, because her gross income exceeds the limit for a qualifying relative
No, because a parent must live in the taxpayer's household
Yes, as a qualifying child
questions.explanation: A parent is within the § 152(d)(2) relationship list without any household requirement, but § 152(d)(1)(B) limits a qualifying relative's gross income to the exemption amount, published for 2026 in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.23, and 7,800 dollars exceeds it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A child lives all year with her mother and her grandmother. The mother has adjusted gross income of 41,000 dollars and the grandmother 29,000 dollars. The mother chooses not to claim the child. May the grandmother?
options: Yes, because the mother has declined the claim
Yes, because the child lived with the grandmother all year
No, because her adjusted gross income does not exceed the mother's
No, because a grandparent can never claim a qualifying child
questions.explanation: Section 152(c)(4)(C) lets a non-parent claim a child the parents could have claimed only if the non-parent's adjusted gross income is higher than the highest of any parent's; declining to claim is not the same as handing the claim over.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Three adult siblings each contribute roughly one-third of their widowed father's support, so none provides over half. Who may claim him as a dependent for the year?
options: Any of them, without further formality
None of them, because no one provides over half of his support
One of them, provided each other sibling contributing over ten percent files a written declaration
All three, each claiming him for one-third of the year
questions.explanation: Under IRC § 152(d)(3) a contributor of over ten percent may be treated as providing over half where the group together does, on condition that every other person contributing over ten percent files a written declaration, arranged before the returns are filed.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer's 20-year-old child lived at home all year, is not a full-time student, and earned $9,000 in wages that the child spent on personal expenses. The taxpayer provided the rest of the child's support. Can the taxpayer claim the child as a dependent?
options: Yes, as a qualifying child, because the child lived at home all year
No, because a 20-year-old who is not a full-time student fails the qualifying child age test and is tested instead as a qualifying relative
Yes, automatically, because the taxpayer provided most of the child's support
No, because the child's own earnings disqualify the taxpayer regardless of the test used
questions.explanation: The qualifying child age test caps at under 19, or under 24 only if a full-time student (or any age if permanently and totally disabled). A 20-year-old non-student fails that test, so the child can only be a dependent as a qualifying relative — which requires the child's gross income to be under the exemption-amount threshold for the year. $9,000 of wages would need to be checked against that threshold before concluding either way; the point tested here is which test applies, not an assumed outcome.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Divorced parents Casey and Jordan do not file a joint return. Their child lived with Casey for 210 nights and with Jordan for 155 nights during the year, and both parents otherwise meet the requirements to claim the child. Absent a signed release (Form 8332) to the contrary, which parent may claim the child as a qualifying child?
options: Jordan, because Jordan has the lower adjusted gross income
Casey, because the child resided with Casey for the greater number of nights
Whichever parent claims the child first on a timely filed return
Neither parent, because the child must be claimed by mutual written agreement
questions.explanation: The tiebreaker rule for divorced or separated parents who don't file jointly awards the qualifying child to the parent with whom the child resided the greater number of nights during the year. Adjusted gross income only becomes the tiebreaker if the nights are exactly equal.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer's elderly parent does not live with the taxpayer but the taxpayer pays for more than half of the parent's total support and the parent's gross income is under the qualifying-relative threshold. What test does the parent NOT need to satisfy that a non-relative living in the home would?
options: The gross income test
The support test
The member-of-household-or-relationship test, as it applies to a member of household requirement
The joint return test
questions.explanation: A qualifying relative must either be related to the taxpayer in one of the specified ways or live with the taxpayer all year as a member of the household. A parent satisfies this through the relationship prong and, unlike an unrelated person, does not also need to live in the taxpayer's home to qualify.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Marisa files her 2026 return using an ITIN. Her dependent son, a citizen with a social security number, is a second-year undergraduate for whom she paid $5,200 of tuition. Which education credit can she claim?
options: The American Opportunity credit, because the student has a social security number
The Lifetime Learning credit only, because it is wholly nonrefundable
Either credit, because an ITIN satisfied the identification rule before 2026 and still does
Neither credit, because the claimant now needs her own social security number
questions.explanation: IRC § 25A(g)(1), as rewritten by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70606(a), requires the individual's social security number rather than any taxpayer identification number, effective for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A preparer's return claims head of household status, the child tax credit, the American Opportunity credit and the Lifetime Learning credit. For which of these does a failure of due diligence carry no preparer penalty under IRC § 6695(g)?
options: Head of household status
The child tax credit
The American Opportunity credit
The Lifetime Learning credit
questions.explanation: IRC § 6695(g)(2) names head of household status and the credits under § 24, § 25A(a)(1) and § 32 only; § 25A(a)(1) is the American Opportunity credit, so the Lifetime Learning credit is outside the rule.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Ines and Tomás file jointly with adjusted gross income high enough to fall in the second reduction band of the 2026 child and dependent care credit. Which describes the applicable percentage under IRC § 21(a)(2) as rewritten?
options: It starts at 35 percent and steps down once to a floor of 20 percent
It starts at 50 percent, steps down to a floor of 35 percent, then steps down again to a floor of 20 percent
It starts at 50 percent and steps down once to a floor of 35 percent
It is a flat 20 percent above the first threshold
questions.explanation: Under IRC § 21(a)(2), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405(a), the percentage starts at 50 percent, loses points to a floor of 35 percent, then loses points again above a second, much higher threshold to a floor of 20 percent; a worked example that opens at 35 percent describes 2025 or earlier.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Beatrix underpaid each of her four 2026 estimated installments. She files her return and pays the full balance due on 27 January 2027. What does that do to the underpayment additions?
options: Removes them for all four installments
Removes the addition for the fourth installment only
Removes nothing, because the return was not filed by the fourth installment's due date
Removes them for the first three installments but not the fourth
questions.explanation: IRC § 6654(h) provides that filing the return and paying in full on or before 31 January removes any underpayment of the fourth installment; the earlier installments are untouched.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of tax payments and refundable credits

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer's earlier earned income credit claim was disallowed after a final determination that it was due to reckless disregard of the rules, not fraud. For how many taxable years after that determination is the credit barred?
options: One
Two
Five
Ten
questions.explanation: IRC § 32(k)(1) bars the credit for a disallowance period of ten taxable years after a final determination of fraud, but two taxable years after a final determination of reckless or intentional disregard.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of tax payments and refundable credits

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Aisha, a citizen all year, filed a full twelve-month 2025 return showing no tax liability. In 2026 she starts a business, owes $14,000 of tax, made no estimated payments and had no withholding. Is she subject to the addition to tax for underpaying estimated tax?
options: Yes, because the tax shown is far above the de minimis amount
Yes, unless she pays in full by 31 January
No, because her prior year was a full twelve months with no liability and she was a citizen throughout
No, because a first-year business is exempt from estimated tax
questions.explanation: IRC § 6654(e)(2) provides that no addition applies where the prior year was a full twelve months, the individual had no liability for it, and was a citizen or resident throughout.
questions.pageTitle: Sources of tax payments and refundable credits

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A client brings in a math error notice dated 45 days ago and asks what can be done. What is the position?
options: Nothing; the only route was a Tax Court petition, and that was never available
A written abatement request is still inside the window, and on receipt the Secretary must abate
The Secretary may abate at its discretion if the request is well founded
The client must pay and then file a claim for refund
questions.explanation: IRC § 6213(b)(2)(A) gives the taxpayer a fixed window from the notice date to request abatement, on which the Secretary shall abate the assessment; any reassessment then follows the ordinary deficiency procedures, which restore the Tax Court route.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which of the following may the Service not assess by the mathematical or clerical error route?
options: An error in multiplication on the return
An entry inconsistent with another entry on the same return
An adjustment to the estimated tax payments credited to the account
A credit exceeding a statutory limit expressed as a monetary amount, where the items applying the limit appear on the return
questions.explanation: IRC § 6213(g)(2)(A)–(H) is a closed list; a correction to withholding or estimated payments is not on it, so it is not a mathematical or clerical error and cannot be assessed by that route.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A lender wants the preparer to speak directly with the IRS about a client's account. The preparer holds a signed Form 8821 for the year. Is that sufficient?
options: Yes, since Form 8821 authorises the preparer to act for the client
No; Form 8821 authorises disclosure only, and a Form 2848 is needed to act as representative
Yes, provided the Form 8821 has been processed by the CAF unit
No; only the client may ever speak with the IRS about the account
questions.explanation: Form 8821 is a tax information authorization, a consent to disclosure under IRC § 6103(c); it does not make the preparer a representative, which takes a Form 2848 power of attorney.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Lorena adds her adult son as joint owner of her home, worth well over the annual exclusion, and describes it as estate planning. Her lifetime exclusion is nowhere near used, so no gift tax is due. Must a gift tax return be filed?
options: No, because no gift tax is due
No, because adding a name to a deed is not a gift
Yes, because IRC § 6019 turns on the transfer, and the exclusion is applied on the return
Only if the son also files a return reporting the gift
questions.explanation: IRC § 6019 requires a return from any individual who makes a transfer by gift in the calendar year, subject only to the listed exceptions, and a transfer of an interest in real property worth far more than the § 2503(b) exclusion is not within them; whether tax is due is a separate question.
questions.pageTitle: Additional required returns filed and taxes paid

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Bruno, a United States citizen, receives the equivalent of 340,000 dollars from his late aunt's estate in Brazil. What is his federal position?
options: The bequest is taxable income and must be reported on Form 1040
Nothing is reportable, because a bequest is excluded from gross income
The bequest is excluded from gross income, but a separate information report of the foreign bequest is required
He must file a gift tax return for the amount received
questions.explanation: IRC § 102(a) excludes a bequest from gross income, but IRC § 6039F separately requires a recipient to report gifts and bequests from certain foreign persons above an annually adjusted aggregate threshold, and 340,000 dollars is far above it; the report produces no tax.
questions.pageTitle: Additional required returns filed and taxes paid

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A client who should have issued a Form 1099 to a contractor neither filed it with the Service nor furnished a statement to the payee. How many penalties are in play?
options: One, for failing to file the information return
One, for failing to furnish the payee statement
Two, separate and cumulative
None, provided the contractor reported the income
questions.explanation: IRC § 6721 penalises the failure to file a correct information return and IRC § 6722 separately penalises the failure to furnish a correct payee statement; the two are cumulative, so one omitted form can be penalised twice.
questions.pageTitle: Additional required returns filed and taxes paid

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A nonresident alien individual has no wages subject to withholding. When is the return due for a calendar year?
options: 15 April
15 June
15 October
The 15th day of the fourth month
questions.explanation: A nonresident alien whose wages *are* subject to chapter 24 withholding files on the ordinary April date.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: What period does IRC § 7508 disregard for a member serving in a combat zone?
options: The period of service only
The period of service plus 90 days
The period of service, plus continuous qualified hospitalisation for an injury received there, plus
One year from the end of service
questions.explanation: and the disregard reaches interest, penalties, additional amounts and additions to tax as well as the filing date.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which extension covers the time to pay as well as the time to file?
options: The automatic six-month extension on Form 4868
The extension for a citizen or resident whose tax home and abode are outside the United States
Any extension requested before the due date
None; extensions never cover payment
questions.explanation: Regulation § 1.6081-5 extends both, and runs concurrently with the six-month extension.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A joint refund is reduced to satisfy one spouse's past-due child support. What is the other spouse's remedy?
options: Innocent spouse relief
An injured spouse claim allocating the joint refund
A collection due process hearing
Nothing; a joint refund is jointly owned
questions.explanation: Innocent spouse relief addresses liability for an understatement, which is a different question.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which statement about disaster relief under IRC § 7508A is correct?
options: Relief is available only where the Secretary issues a notice
There is both a discretionary period the Secretary may specify and a mandatory period
The liability is forgiven, not postponed
Relief applies only to the filing date, not to payment
questions.explanation: The mandatory period operates on the declaration's own dates whether or not a notice issues.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A joint refund faces three claims: past-due child support certified by a State, a federal non-tax debt, and a State income tax obligation. Under IRC § 6402(c), which reduction is applied first?
options: The federal non-tax debt
The State-certified past-due support
The State income tax obligation
They are applied pro rata
questions.explanation: IRC § 6402(c) directs the Secretary to reduce the overpayment by State-certified past-due support and to apply that reduction first, before other reductions allowed by law.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Corporal Ines returns from a designated combat zone and asks whether she must file Form 4868 to obtain the postponement of her filing deadline. What is the correct advice?
options: Yes, an extension request must be filed before the original due date
Yes, but the request may be filed within 180 days after leaving the zone
No, the period is disregarded by operation of the statute and no request is required
No, but she must attach a written statement to the return explaining the delay
questions.explanation: Section 7508(a) disregards the period by operation of the statute; filing an extension request is harmless but unnecessary, and advising a client that they must apply misstates the relief.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Hana, a citizen whose tax home and abode are in Singapore, qualifies for the extension in Reg. § 1.6081-5 and also files an ordinary six-month extension request. How long does she have to file?
options: Six months from the ordinary April due date, because the two extensions run concurrently
Six months after the abroad extension ends, because the two run in sequence
Only to the fifteenth day of the sixth month, because the abroad extension displaces any other
Only to the ordinary April date, because a taxpayer abroad must choose one extension
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6081-5 extends the time to the fifteenth day of the sixth month following the close of the year, and the ordinary six-month extension runs concurrently with it rather than after it.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A United States person has signature authority over a foreign account belonging to their employer, with no financial interest in it. What must they file?
options: Neither the FBAR nor Form 8938
The FBAR only
Form 8938 only
Both
questions.explanation: The FBAR reaches signature or other authority over an account; § 6038D reaches an interest in an asset.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: When is the FBAR due?
options: 30 June, with no extension available
15 April, with an automatic extension to 15 October that need not be requested
With the income tax return, including any extension
31 December of the year reported
questions.explanation: The regulation at 31 C.F.R. § 1010.306(c) still states 30 June and is superseded.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An unmarried taxpayer living in the United States held foreign assets worth $72,000 in July and $8,000 on 31 December. Is Form 8938 required?
options: No; the last-day value is below the threshold
Yes; the any-time value exceeds $75,000
No; the any-time value is below $75,000 and the last-day value is below $50,000
Yes; any foreign asset must be reported
questions.explanation: Both tests are below their thresholds — $72,000 does not exceed $75,000, and $8,000 does not exceed $50,000.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which is not reportable on an FBAR?
options: A foreign brokerage account producing no income
A foreign account emptied before year end
An account held in an IRA of which the taxpayer is the owner
A foreign account over which the taxpayer has only signature authority
questions.explanation: Accounts held in an IRA or a retirement plan of which the person is owner, beneficiary or participant are among the categories the IRS lists as not reportable.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Where is the FBAR filed?
options: Attached to the federal income tax return
With the IRS service centre for the taxpayer's district
Electronically with FinCEN through the BSA E-Filing System
With the Department of State
questions.explanation: It is not filed with the tax return.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An unmarried taxpayer living in the United States holds one foreign brokerage account worth about 120,000 dollars throughout the year, and has no other foreign assets. What must she file?
options: The FBAR only, since one filing covers the account
Form 8938 only, since the account is reported on the return
Both the FBAR with FinCEN and Form 8938 attached to the return
Neither, because the account is held at a financial institution
questions.explanation: The account exceeds the FBAR trigger under 31 C.F.R. § 1010.350(a) and the Form 8938 thresholds in Reg. § 1.6038D-2(a) for an unmarried individual living in the United States, and there is no coordination letting one filing satisfy the other, so the same asset is reported to two agencies.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A married couple living abroad files jointly. Their foreign accounts were worth 250,000 dollars on 31 December and peaked at 320,000 dollars in August. Must they attach Form 8938?
options: Yes, on the last-day test
Yes, on the any-time test
No, both values are below the threshold pair for a joint return filed from abroad, though an FBAR is still due
No, because taxpayers living abroad are outside IRC § 6038D
questions.explanation: Reg. § 1.6038D-2(a) sets a separate, higher threshold pair for married taxpayers filing jointly and living abroad, and neither the last-day value nor the highest value during the year exceeds it; the FBAR under 31 C.F.R. § 1010.350(a) is still required because the aggregate value exceeded its trigger at some time in the year.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A lawful permanent resident who is not a United States citizen holds a foreign bank account worth about 40,000 dollars that produced no income during the year. Is she required to file an FBAR?
options: No, because the FBAR applies only to citizens
No, because the account produced no income
Yes, because a resident alien is a United States person and income is irrelevant
Only if she also meets the Form 8938 threshold
questions.explanation: Under 31 C.F.R. § 1010.350(b) a United States person includes a resident, being a resident alien under IRC § 7701(b), and the IRS states that whether the account produced taxable income has no effect on whether it is reportable.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which child is not subject to the kiddie tax?
options: A 16-year-old with substantial earned income and unearned income above the threshold
A 19-year-old full-time student whose earned income is one-third of their support
A 22-year-old full-time student whose earned income exceeds one-half of their support
A 12-year-old whose parents are both alive
questions.explanation: The earned income comparison applies to the over-18 limb, and exceeding half of support takes the child outside the rule; a child under 18 is within it regardless of earnings.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: How much unearned income may a child have in 2026 before any of it is taxed at the parent's rate?
questions.explanation: The definition of net unearned income subtracts the § 63(c)(5)(A) amount twice where the child does not itemise.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Income between the dependent standard deduction floor and the kiddie tax threshold is taxed at what rate?
options: Zero
The child's own rate
The parent's rate
The trust and estate rate
questions.explanation: Only net unearned income above the threshold reaches the parent's rate.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A child's only income is $6,000 of dividends, and backup withholding was applied to the account. May the parent elect to report the income on their own return?
options: Yes; the income is within the range and is only dividends
No; the election is unavailable where any amount has been withheld under the backup withholding
Yes, if the withholding is refunded first
Only if the child is under 18
questions.explanation: and the child should file anyway, because the withheld tax is recoverable only on the child's return.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Two children of the same parent each have net unearned income. How is the allocable parental tax computed?
options: Separately for each child
Once, on the parent's income including the net unearned income of all affected children, then
Only for the child with the larger amount
By adding the children's own tax liabilities
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 15-year-old has 9,000 dollars of dividend income and no earned income. Both of her parents died in March of the year. Is her net unearned income taxed at a parent's rate for the year?
options: Yes, because she is under 18
Yes, using the rate of the parent who died last
No, because neither parent is alive at the close of the taxable year
No, because the trust and estate rate schedule applies instead
questions.explanation: Section 1(g)(2) requires all three conditions to hold, including that either parent be alive at the close of the taxable year; with no living parent the rule does not apply, and the trust rate schedule was repealed by the SECURE Act of 2019.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 12-year-old has 3,200 dollars of interest and 600 dollars of capital gain from selling shares, with no withholding or estimated payments in her name. May her parent make the election to report her income on the parent's return?
options: Yes, because the total is within the election range
Yes, if the capital gain is reported separately by the child
No, because the election requires that the child's income be only interest and dividends
No, because the election is available only for children under 10
questions.explanation: The § 1(g)(7) election is available only where the child's income is only interest and dividends, within the stated range, with no estimated payments or backup withholding in the child's name; a capital gain takes the child outside it, and a return must be filed for the child.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 10-year-old with no earned income and no itemised deductions has 5,000 dollars of unearned income in 2026. Both parents are alive and she files no joint return. How much is taxed at the parent's rate?
options: 5,000 dollars
3,650 dollars
2,300 dollars
1,350 dollars
questions.explanation: Under § 1(g)(4)(A) net unearned income is unearned income reduced by the § 63(c)(5)(A) floor of 1,350 dollars twice where the child does not itemise; the first 1,350 is absorbed by the standard deduction, the next 1,350 is taxed at the child's own rate, and the remaining 2,300 reaches the parent's rate.
questions.pageTitle: Minor children's unearned income — the kiddie tax

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 16-year-old dependent has $4,000 of interest income and no earned income for the year. Which statement about the kiddie tax rules is correct?
options: The kiddie tax cannot apply because the child is under 18
The kiddie tax can apply because the child is under 18 at year end, regardless of earned income
The kiddie tax only applies once the child turns 18
The kiddie tax applies only if the child files a joint return
questions.explanation: The kiddie tax age test is met for any child under age 18 at year end, without regard to how much earned income the child has. (The earned-income-versus-support comparison only comes into play for the 18, and 19–23 full-time student, age brackets.)

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 19-year-old, full-time college student who is a dependent has $6,000 of earned income and $3,000 of unearned income, and the earned income is more than half of the student's own support for the year. Does the kiddie tax apply?
options: Yes, because the student is under 24
No, because a full-time student age 19–23 is only subject to the kiddie tax if earned income does NOT exceed half of the student's own support, and here it does
Yes, because the student has any unearned income at all
No, full-time students are always exempt from the kiddie tax
questions.explanation: For the 19–23 full-time-student bracket, the kiddie tax age test is met only when the student's earned income does NOT exceed half of their own support. Because this student's earned income does exceed half of their support, the age test for this bracket is not met, so the kiddie tax does not apply on that basis.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Parents want to report their young child's interest and dividend income directly on their own return instead of filing a separate return for the child. Which form supports that election, and which form is used if the parents do not make it?
options: Form 8814 to elect to include the child's income on the parents' return; Form 8615 on the child's own return if the election is not made
Form 8615 to elect to include the child's income on the parents' return; Form 8814 on the child's own return if the election is not made
Form 8332 for either option, depending on custodial status
Schedule 8812 for either option, depending on the amount of income
questions.explanation: Form 8814 (Parents' Election to Report Child's Interest and Dividends) lets qualifying parents include the child's investment income on their own return. If the parents don't make that election — or the child doesn't qualify for it — the child's own return computes the kiddie tax using Form 8615.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Which form reports health insurance obtained from a source other than the Marketplace?
options: Form 1095-A
Form 1095-B
Form 1095-C
All of these
questions.explanation: Form 1095-A comes from the Marketplace; Form 1095-C comes from an applicable large employer.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: What is the individual shared responsibility payment for 2026?
options: It is computed as a percentage of household income
It is the greater of a flat dollar amount or a percentage of income
Zero, because both limbs of the penalty computation now yield nothing
The requirement to maintain coverage was repealed, so there is none
questions.explanation: The requirement in § 5000A remains; only the penalty amounts were reduced to zero.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A taxpayer's household income is 415 percent of the poverty line for their family size in 2026, and they received advance premium tax credit payments. What follows?
options: A reduced credit computed on a percentage of income
No credit, and the advance payments are repayable
The credit is unaffected, because the ceiling was suspended
The credit is available but capped at the advance payments
questions.explanation: The suspension of the 400 percent ceiling applied only to taxable years beginning before 1 January 2026.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: Excess advance premium tax credit payments in 2026 are repaid in what amount?
options: Limited by a cap that varies with household income
In full, regardless of household income
Only to the extent they exceed the credit by more than a stated amount
Not at all, if income was correctly projected at enrolment
questions.explanation: The limitation in § 36B(f)(2)(B) was removed for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: An employer averaged exactly 50 full-time employees during the preceding calendar year. Is it an applicable large employer?
options: No; the threshold is more than 50
Yes; the threshold is an average of at least 50
Only if it offers coverage
Only if the employees are in a single location

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A 20-year-old full-time student who lives at home and whom her parents are entitled to claim enrolls in Marketplace coverage in her own name. Her own income for 2026 is modest. May she claim the premium tax credit on her own return?
options: Yes, because her income sits inside the poverty-line range
Yes, provided her parents do not also claim it
No, because a dependent of another taxpayer cannot be an applicable taxpayer
No, because students are excluded from Marketplace coverage
questions.explanation: Section 36B(c)(1)(D) denies applicable-taxpayer status to anyone who is another taxpayer's dependent for the year, however low her income runs.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A married couple enrolled through the Marketplace and received advance payments during 2026. They decide to file separate returns for the year. What is the consequence for the premium tax credit?
options: Each spouse claims half of the credit on their separate return
The credit is computed on the higher-earning spouse's return only
Neither spouse is an applicable taxpayer, so no credit is allowed
The credit is unaffected as long as household income is within the range
questions.explanation: Under § 36B(c)(1)(C), married taxpayers must file a joint return to be applicable taxpayers; filing separately forecloses the credit.

questions.sectionTitle: Preliminary work to prepare tax returns
questions.stem: A Marketplace enrollee's household income sits at about 250 percent of the poverty line in both 2025 and 2026, on otherwise identical facts. How does the 2026 credit compare with 2025?
options: It is the same, because the income range is unchanged
It is smaller, because the temporary premium percentages lapsed for taxable years beginning after 2025
It is larger, because the repayment limitation was removed
There is no credit in 2026, because the ceiling was restored
